1 
INFR11269 Coursework video production guide 
Make a clear screen recording with narration, trim it if needed, and check the exported file before 
submission. This guide provides a practical workflow; the submission requirements specify the 
assessed content, timing and anonymity rules. 
Choose a simple workflow 
Use a recorder or editor you already know, or try the free tools below. You only need an editor if you 
want to join or trim clips, and a compressor if your exported file is too large. All three tools are 
available for Windows, macOS and Linux. 
•   OBS Studio   —   record your screen and microphone. 
•   Shotcut   —   trim recordings, join clips and export the finished video. 
•   HandBrake   —   re - encode the finished video to reduce its file size. 
Download from these official websites. No paid software is needed for this workflow. 
Prepare the screen and a short outline 
Plan up to eight minutes for the presentation and system demonstration, followed by the final two 
minutes for the two released questions. Keep the complete video within ten minutes. A few slides and 
a readable terminal or application window are enough. 
Use an anonymous project title. Close email and messaging apps, turn off notifications, hide personal 
account names and file paths, and keep API keys and other credentials off screen. Use narration 
without webcam footage. Enlarge terminal text and figures before recording. 
Prepare the demonstration input and configuration, and practise showing the command or action, the 
actual run and its output. Explain what the result demonstrates. If recording affects system 
performance, explain results using your separately measured experiments rather than treating the 
recording as a timing benchmark. 
Record with OBS Studio 
1. Open Tools > Auto - Configuration Wizard and choose recording as your purpose. In the Sources 
panel, add Window Capture or Display Capture on Windows/Linux, or macOS Screen Capture on 
macOS. Grant screen and microphone permissions if prompted. 
2. Select your microphone in Settings > Audio and check that its meter moves. Mute unwanted 
desktop sound. A headset can help avoid echo. Make a short test recording and play it back to check 
sound, screen capture and readable text. 
3. Try 1920 × 1080 at 30 frames per second as a starting point, if your screen and computer support it. 
Record only the area you need. These are practical suggestions, not submission requirements. 
4. Start Recording, present your work, then Stop Recording. You can record separate sections if that 
makes mistakes easier to correct. For an MKV recording, use File > Remux Recordings to create an 
MP4 for editing; remuxing changes the container without reducing video quality or substantially 
shrinking the file. 
Help:   OBS quick start   and   recording formats

2 
Trim and join clips with Shotcut 
Create a project, open your recording and drag it onto the Timeline. Drag a clip edge to trim its start 
or end. To remove a mistake in the middle, split at either side of it, remove the unwanted section and 
close the gap. Arrange any separate recordings in presentation order. 
Keep edits simple. If you shorten a wait during the system demonstration, make the cut clear, for 
example with a brief “Waiting time shortened” caption. Keep the input, configuration and resulting 
output understandable. Put both question answers in the final two - minute section and introduce them 
as Question 1 and Question 2. 
Save the editing project, then use Export to produce an MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio. The 
project file is not the submitted video. Watch the export to check for gaps, missing audio and 
accidental cuts. 
Help:   Shotcut tutorials, including exporting 
Reduce file size with HandBrake if needed 
Check the upload limit published on Learn first. If your file already meets it and plays well, further 
compression is unnecessary. Keep the original export so you can retry without repeatedly 
compressing an already compressed copy. 
1. Open the exported video in HandBrake. Select the Fast 1080p30 preset, which uses MP4, H.264 
video and AAC audio. Choose a new output filename. 
2. Start with the preset’s quality setting. Inspect the dimensions and cropping preview so terminal text 
or window edges are not removed. Encode a short preview containing your smallest text and listen to 
the narration. 
3. If the file remains too large, increase the RF value for the H.264 (x264) encoder by a small amount, 
such as two points, and test again. A higher RF reduces quality and generally reduces size. Constant 
quality does not guarantee a particular file size. 
4. Try Fast 720p30 only if text remains readable at the lower resolution. Once satisfied, encode the 
whole video, compare its size with the upload limit and watch the final file. Compression settings 
cannot recover detail that was unreadable in the recording. 
Help:   HandBrake presets   and   adjusting quality 
Check the file you will submit 
•   Duration is at most ten minutes, including the final two minutes for both questions; the actual 
system demonstration is present. 
•   Narration is audible throughout; code, plots and outputs remain readable in the final compressed 
video. Check captions for errors if you include them. 
•   No names, UUNs, Group IDs, faces, identifying credits or credentials appear. Check the video’s 
title/author metadata as well as visible content. Use a neutral filename such as video.mp4. 
•   Submit through the route specified on Learn. Allow time for upload and processing, then check 
playback or download the submitted file to confirm it is the intended version. 
Use materials you have permission to include 
Your own slides, figures, screen recording and narration are usually all you need. For third - party 
images, music or clips, check that your use is permitted and provide any required credit. Downloading 
a free editor does not grant permission to reuse someone else’s media. 
Further guidance:   UK copyright guidance
